20261118-chemistry-g05.s.s1.explain: Water, the substance that dissolves things, is the 'solvent,' sugar, which dissolves, is the 'solute,' and the clear mixture in which the two are evenly mixed is called the 'solution.'

20261119-chemistry-g05.s.s1.hint.0: A solution is a 'homogeneous mixture' in which the particles are evenly mixed at the molecular level.

20261121-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.prompt: When salt is added to 100 g of water, why does more salt dissolve when the water temperature is 60℃ than when it is 20℃?

20261121-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.hint.0: Recall the curve of solubility change with temperature.
20261121-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.hint.1: The warmer it is, the more active the molecular motion of the matter.

20261121-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.o.o1: Because high temperature destroys the molecular structure of salt

20261121-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.prompt: A cherry tomato was put in a tank of plain water and sank to the bottom. After a generous amount of salt was added to the tank and stirred, the cherry tomato floated up to the surface. Why?
20261121-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.explain: Salt water is denser than plain water, and when salt keeps dissolving until the density of the salt water becomes greater than the average density of the cherry tomato, the buoyant force becomes greater than gravity and the tomato floats up.
20261121-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.hint.0: If the density of a liquid is greater than the density of an object, the object floats up.
20261121-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.hint.1: The more salt dissolves, the greater the weight (density) of the liquid.

20261122-chemistry-g05-1.material: [Advanced Crystallization] A saturated solution was made by dissolving alum in warm water at 60℃ until no more would dissolve, a silk thread was hung in this solution, and it was slowly cooled at room temperature, and beautiful gem-shaped alum crystals grew on the silk thread. What is the principle behind this phenomenon?
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced Crystallization] A saturated solution was made by dissolving alum in warm water at 60℃ until no more would dissolve, a silk thread was hung in this solution, and it was slowly cooled at room temperature, and beautiful gem-shaped alum crystals grew on the silk thread. What is the principle behind this phenomenon?
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.explain: When the temperature falls, the solubility of a solid decreases sharply, so the supersaturated solute that was dissolved in an amount greater than the lowered solubility joins together into regular crystals and comes out, which is the phenomenon of 'recrystallization (precipitation).'
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.hint.0: What happens when a solid that was dissolved in large amounts while warm cools down?
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.hint.1: When the temperature drops and the solubility becomes smaller, it is pushed out (precipitation).
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.o.o0: Because as the temperature falls, the solubility of alum decreases, and the amount that can no longer stay dissolved separates out as solid crystals
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.o.o1: Because the alum solution froze into ice
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.o.o2: Because the silk thread chemically synthesized alum
20261122-chemistry-g05-1.s.s1.o.o3: Because dust in the air turned into alum

20261122-chemistry-g05-2.thinking.0: What is the scientific principle by which
20261122-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.prompt: What is the scientific principle by which, when you open the lid of a can of a cold carbonated drink (cider or cola), there is a 'psst' sound and bubbles actively rise in the drink?
20261122-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.explain: The carbon dioxide gas that was dissolved in large amounts in the water under the high pressure inside the sealed can comes out as bubbles, because when the lid is opened and the pressure drops, its solubility decreases according to Henry's law.
20261122-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.hint.1: The solubility of a gas increases at higher pressure and decreases when the pressure drops.
20261122-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.o.o0: Because when the can is opened, the internal pressure drops to atmospheric pressure, and the solubility of carbon dioxide gas decreases sharply
20261122-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.o.o1: Because when the can is opened, the temperature of the drink suddenly drops below zero
20261122-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.o.o2: Because the water in the drink evaporates instantly
20261122-chemistry-g05-2.s.s1.o.o3: Because oxygen in the air is sucked into the drink

20261119-chemistry-g06.s.s1.prompt: When dilute hydrochloric acid or vinegar was dropped onto eggshell or a piece of marble (containing calcium carbonate), bubbles fizzed up. What change occurs when this gas is collected and passed through limewater?

20261119-chemistry-g06.s.s1.hint.1: When carbon dioxide is passed through limewater, a calcium carbonate precipitate forms and makes it cloudy.

20261119-chemistry-g06.s.s1.o.o1: When a flame is held to the limewater, it burns with a pop
20261119-chemistry-g06.s.s1.o.o2: The color of the limewater turns blue

20261121-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.prompt: What is the scientific principle behind the household wisdom of sprinkling lemon juice or vinegar when cooking fish in order to get rid of the fishy smell (trimethylamine and similar compounds, which are basic)?
20261121-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.explain: Amines, the cause of the fishy smell of fish, are basic, so when an acidic substance such as lemon juice (citric acid) or vinegar (acetic acid) is sprinkled on, an acid-base neutralization reaction occurs and the fishy smell disappears.
20261121-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.hint.0: When an acid and a base meet, a 'neutralization reaction' occurs in which each loses its properties.

20261121-chemistry-g06-2.steps.0.explain: Covering a fire with sand or a thick blanket, or spraying it with a carbon dioxide extinguisher, puts out the fire by completely cutting off the inflow of oxygen, which is the 'smothering' method.
20261121-chemistry-g06-2.steps.0.hints.0: The three elements of combustion: combustible material, oxygen, and a temperature at or above the ignition point
20261121-chemistry-g06-2.steps.0.hints.1: If you cover it with sand, air cannot reach the flame.
20261121-chemistry-g06-2.steps.0.options.0.text: Cutting off the supply of oxygen in the air (smothering)
20261121-chemistry-g06-2.steps.0.options.1.text: Completely removing the combustible material (firewood) itself

20261122-chemistry-g06-1.title: Advanced Reaction Reasoning
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.goal: تطبيق مبادئ Advanced Reaction Reasoning لحل مسألة التفكير والاستقصاء.
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.material: [Advanced Reaction Reasoning] Dilute hydrochloric acid was added little by little with a dropper to a sodium hydroxide solution, which turns red litmus paper blue, and mixed. Which describes the change that occurs in the mixed solution when a sufficient amount of hydrochloric acid has been added?
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.prompt: [Advanced Reaction Reasoning] Dilute hydrochloric acid was added little by little with a dropper to a sodium hydroxide solution, which turns red litmus paper blue, and mixed. Which describes the change that occurs in the mixed solution when a sufficient amount of hydrochloric acid has been added?
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.explain: When an acid (hydrochloric acid) and a base (sodium hydroxide) react, water and a salt are produced and heat of neutralization is released, so the temperature rises. If hydrochloric acid is added in excess, the entire solution becomes acidic and turns blue litmus paper red.
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.hint.0: In a neutralization reaction, heat of neutralization is released and the temperature rises.
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.hint.1: If hydrochloric acid is added in excess, it becomes an acidic solution.
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.o.o0: Heat is released and the temperature rises, and the final solution turns blue litmus paper red
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.o.o1: The solution suddenly becomes cold and turns into ice
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.o.o2: No reaction occurs at all and it stays as it was
20261122-chemistry-g06-1.s.s1.o.o3: Only hydrogen gas is produced explosively

20261122-chemistry-g06-2.title: When a large forest fire is spreading
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.topic: When a large forest fire is spreading
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.goal: تطبيق مبادئ When a large forest fire is spreading لحل مسألة التفكير والاستقصاء.
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.material: When a large forest fire is spreading, cutting down the trees ahead of the fire's path widely with chainsaws in advance to build a 'firebreak' removes which of the three elements of combustion?
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.thinking.0: When a large forest fire is spreading
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.s.s1.prompt: When a large forest fire is spreading, cutting down the trees ahead of the fire's path widely with chainsaws in advance to build a 'firebreak' removes which of the three elements of combustion?
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.s.s1.explain: This is the removal method of fire suppression, which stops a forest fire from spreading by removing in advance the 'combustible material,' one of the essential elements of combustion, so that there is no fuel to burn in the path the flames are advancing along.
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.s.s1.hint.0: For a fire to keep burning, combustible material must stay continuously connected.
20261122-chemistry-g06-2.s.s1.hint.1: If the trees are removed in advance, the fire has nowhere left to spread.
